children: DFI Retail Group has agreed to sell its 50% stake in Maxim's Caterers in exchange for the latter's Starbucks Asia business and about $340 million in cash.
After the deal, DFI will take over the Starbucks operations in Hong Kong, Macau, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam, Cambodia and Laos, comprising more than 1,100 stores.
Maxim's has been Starbucks' licensing partner in the region since 2000, when the partnership began in Hong Kong before expanding to other markets.
Maxim's will buy back DFI's 50% stake, according to an exchange filling Wednesday. The transaction is expected to be completed by end-March 2027.
The Starbucks business generated about $750 million in revenue in 2025,  with an underlying operating margin of 7.0%.
The Starbucks business is expected to contribute $600 to $650 million to DFI's total subsidiaries' revenue from April to December 2027, it said.
DFI raised its 2027 dividend payout ratio to 80%, supporting continued growth in dividend per share, and maintained its 2028 underlying profit guidance of $310 million to $350 million.
